questions.question: How did cameras and photographs change from the first photographs to today?
questions.expected_answer: The first photographs, made in the 1820s, took hours, and in 1839 they took minutes, so people had to sit very still. From 1888, Kodak sold small cameras with roll film, so ordinary people could take photos, but film had to be developed in a darkroom. In 1975, the first digital camera was built, and today cameras are built into cell phones.

questions.question: How does a cell phone work, and when did cell phones come to South Africa?
questions.expected_answer: A cell phone sends and receives radio waves. The country is divided into small areas called cells, each with a tower or mast. The phone sends radio waves to the nearest tower, which passes the call through the network to the other person. Cell phones came to South Africa in 1994.

questions.question: Give two ways cell phones have made life better and two problems they can cause.
questions.expected_answer: Better: people can contact family anywhere at any time; video calls and photos keep families close; people in rural areas can make calls; phones help in emergencies and for sending money, learning and news. Problems: phones and data cost money; too much screen time; cyberbullying and false information; personal photos and information can be shared; phones can be stolen.
